## Answer transaction and task cost

- **Accepted mark:** queued/delivered/replay role responses receive an in-process typed Response extension; send/shim inspect that mark, not HTTP 200. It adds constant-size marker/lookup work, no serialized response-body reread, SQL or process. A refused holder receipt remains unmarked and skips answer accounting.
- **Caller refusal:** unresolved supplied context now returns the identity ladder's refusal, instead of constructing unbound evidence and proceeding. It reuses existing identity/registry/liveness reads; no new lookup loop or launch site. No-context-at-all remains the separate accepted residual.
- **Accounting:** the existing primary-key request read still checks delivered state and stored holder. A qualifying audited reply enters publish_committed_batch, with one owned publication task and the store's owned write inside it. A schema-checked transaction performs the keyed unanswered-only UPDATE and, only if changed, **one request.answered_by_reply INSERT**, then COMMIT and broadcast.
- **Atomicity:** there is no longer a second standalone audit transaction after an answer committed. An append failure rolls back the stamp; it is logged and the send itself retains its existing result. A later reply may retry accounting. No new automatic retry, timer or poll.
- **Duplicates:** an already-answered eligible request can still pay the request read, publication-lock wait and a no-change transaction, but appends no second event. Output --answers shares the same answered_at field. Noneligible/refused replies do not enter the answer write.

The global publication-order lock now covers schema/answer transaction work before broadcast; concurrent answers can queue behind other event writers. The store helper returns its stamped flag/events directly, without a post-commit request reload under that lock. Metadata copies/serialization and one retained audit row scale per newly stamped answer and evidence bytes. Full request body materialization by the existing request read remains; the audit payload carries no body.

This is **one transaction per answer-accounting attempt**, not one total transaction per complete send: role-request admission, message delivery/FYI holding and their existing persistence can add work. Ownership means an admitted mutation/broadcast survives a dropped waiter; it is not a whole-runtime crash or bounded-latency guarantee.

No new executable site, recurring task, poll or timer in the fix. Rates follow accepted correlated replies, not seats per watchdog tick. Previous per-message CPU/model-round costs, member retention, claim renewal, held-query/cardinality and live-proof limits remain.

## Proof and C32 scope

Exact-head CI executes **a_reply_answer_and_its_audit_commit_together_or_not_at_all**: an audit-only abort trigger leaves no stamp/event; retry stamps once; replay and output --answers leave one timestamp/event. The HTTP regression covers refused role receipts on send/shim, contradicted supplied context, and a matching-holder positive control. These close the old best-effort accounting proof gap without a local trigger.

That supports clarified **C32(3)**'s atomic asserted-identity accounting. Herring owns the full C32 signal-only/binding/exact-Known-limit grade, especially whether any message can be delivered as another seat; this cost pass does not endorse that separate condition.
